summary: Unexpected autoscale throttles causing transient GPU shortages during evening peak window
description:
Issue summary:
During the customer evening peak (approx 19:00-20:15 UTC) Textly.ai observed repeated P99 throughput regressions for routes pinned to their dedicated pool. Symptoms included elevated request queueing, autoscaler throttles (rate-limit style rejection of new GPU allocations), and a short-lived shortage of free GPU slots that recovered after ~8-10 minutes.

Impact:
- Customer-facing latency p99 increased from ~180ms to 1.2s for generation routes for ~35% of requests during the window.
- A subset of small, high-concurrency streams experienced preemptive queuing and a spike in 503s when allocation throttles triggered.
- Business impact: degraded UX for Textly.ai paying customers (estimated 1.2k affected requests in window).

Environment:
- Dedicated pool: dp-textly-prod-us-east (configured min_replicas=2, max_replicas=10, burst_capacity=2)
- Region: us-east-1
- Models: redwood-v2-large (primary), fallback to open-llama-13B for cost-tier routes
- Autoscaler: adaptive-burst (policy version 2026-02-18)

Steps to reproduce (observed pattern):
1) High rate of short-lived concurrent streams from customer traffic (many requests <200 tokens, duration <2s) starting 19:03 UTC.
2) Autoscaler began requesting new GPU allocation for additional slots; allocation requests hit quota soft-limit enforced by internal allocator for the dedicated pool.
3) Allocator returned throttled responses for ~6 minutes; requests were queued locally in the router.
4) Some queued requests exceeded route timeouts and returned 503/504.
5) Once some longer-running background workloads finished or preempted, allocations succeeded and queue drained by 19:11 UTC.

Observed logs and metrics (snippet):
- metrics/autoscaler/alloc_retries: spike from 3->47 in 3 minutes
- allocator/errors: rate_limit_exceeded (internal quota) 78 events between 19:04-19:08 UTC
- serving/runtime/gpu_util: per-GPU 92-98% during peak, but slot free-count reported transiently 0/64 for 7 minutes
- router/queue_length: p95 from 2 -> 18 requests
- customer reported 503s correlated with allocator throttle timestamps (see attached traces).

Expected behavior:
- Autoscaler should either succeed or fall back to graceful degradation policies (route-level fallbacks to cheaper model or enqueue into burst buffer) without triggering quota-throttle that causes abrupt 503s.

Initial triage:
- Hypothesis 1: Background scheduled batch/maintenance task on same dedicated cluster caused temporary GPU bank contention and reduced capacity; autoscaler escalated but was throttled by allocator quota.
- Hypothesis 2: Adaptive-burst autoscaler misestimated warmup time for additional GPU nodes leading to a cascade of allocation requests that tripped internal rate limits.
- Hypothesis 3: Noisy neighbor from other tenants in the same host-pool performing short high-concurrency streams causing slot fragmentation.

Attachments:
- packet: trace-Textly-2026-03-12-19-03.json (router traces)
- grafana: panels (autoscaler, allocator errors, gpu_util, queue_length)

Requested by customer:
Customer requests immediate mitigation (reduce p99 latency) and post-incident follow-up to avoid recurrence. They prefer isolation if needed (pin to reserved machines for peak hours).
comments: 2026-03-12 | Support (Ava Martinez): Ticket created after Textly support alerted #support. Collecting traces and metrics; escalated to SRE oncall.

2026-03-12 | SRE (Morgan Li): Confirmed allocator rate_limit_exceeded spikes in grafana. Opening temporary mitigation: increase allocator soft quota for dp-textly-prod-us-east by +2 for 1 hour. Applied at 19:22 UTC; queue drained by 19:30 UTC.
2026-03-12 | Customer (Textly.ai - Priya Shah): Thanks. We saw improvement after your change. Can we get a permanent fix? Peak hours are predictable for us (18:30-20:30 UTC).
2026-03-13 | Product (Diego Ramos): Suggest adding scheduled reservation window feature for dedicated pools or policy to pre-warm GPUs for customers with predictable peaks. Filing product follow-up.

2026-03-14 | SRE (Morgan Li): Running deeper analysis; correlating cluster maintenance events and background batch jobs. Found 1 host with nightly checkpoint writer that overlapped with peak and had I/O causing transient kernel backpressure.
investigation_notes: 2026-03-12 20:00 UTC - Found allocator throttle window aligns with a short burst of 120 small concurrent streams from tenant 'content-ml' sharing same host-pool.
2026-03-12 21:10 UTC - Node-level logs show kernel-level IO wait spikes on host xg-pool-13 causing slower container eviction and delayed slot freeing.

2026-03-13 09:00 UTC - Autoscaler policy 2026-02-18 uses conservative warmup timeout (45s) but issues parallel allocation requests; this interacts poorly with our allocator's per-minute allocation limit and causes aggregated throttles.
2026-03-13 11:40 UTC - Confirmed no scheduled cluster maintenance in region during that window; but a tenant scheduled checkpoint job started at 19:02 (cron job mis-scheduled).

2026-03-14 10:30 UTC - Reproduced high-concurrency short-stream load in staging and observed allocation throttling when allocator soft quota set to default. We reproduced queueing and p99 blips similar to production.
resolution_notes: Mitigation applied (temporary): increased allocator soft quota for dp-textly-prod-us-east by +2 replicas at 19:22 UTC on 2026-03-12; removed after stability confirmed at 20:00 UTC.
Short-term plan: schedule tenant isolation for predictable peak windows (Textly advised to request reservation for 18:30-20:30 UTC) — SRE to create reservation for next 14 days.

Medium-term: autoscaler tuning - change parallel allocation backoff and add jitter to reduce simultaneous allocation fanout; target PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/autoscaler/pull/489 (under review).
Long-term: product feature - scheduled reservation/pre-warm API for dedicated pools and allocator rate-limit control per-customer. Product to own roadmap item.

Follow-ups: 1) SRE to identify and quarantine noisy tenant 'content-ml' daily checkpoint job; 2) Reduce default allocator parallelism threshold for adaptive-burst policy; 3) Add alert for allocator.rate_limit_exceeded > 5/min.
Status: In Progress - mitigation successful, customer stable; implementing medium-term autoscaler change and creating reservation as requested.
